A Roughneck (Japanese: スキンヘッズ Skinheads), known as a Cue Ball until Generation IV, is a type of Pokémon Trainer introduced in Generation I. They appear as bald men wearing leather jackets. Roughnecks can be commonly found in the vicinity of s and, in Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!, s. In Sinnoh, they have a on the back of their vest; in Unova, they have a . Cue Ball may be referring to their bald heads, which can resemble white billiards balls.

They are sometimes depicted as being affiliated with Team Rocket.

When paired with s in Double Battles, they are called .

They specialize in Pokémon in Generations I and III, and in in Generation V. In the Battle Subway, they specialize in Pokémon with one-hit knockout moves and, in the early stages, Dark- and Fighting-type Pokémon.

In Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!, Roughnecks award three s along with prize money upon being defeated.

==In animation==
 
A Roughneck by the name of appeared in Rocking the Virbank Gym! Part 1 and Part 2. He is the drummer in Roxie's rock band " and the Toxics".
 

==In the manga==
===Pokémon Adventures===
 
 
====History====
===== =====
A Roughneck appears seen amongst the people at the Johto Safari Zone in Weavile Wobbles But It Won't Fall Down.

===== =====
In Bombastic Bibarel & Heroic Hippopotas, a Roughneck appeared at the Seven Stars Restaurant.

In Vexing Vespiquen & Unmanageable Mothim I, and Riley encountered two Roughnecks hired by Team Galactic to disrupt their progressing. The Roughnecks took 's Egg as a hostage but were eventually outsmarted by Diamond.

===== =====
A Roughneck was seen in Deprogramming Porygon-Z, entering the after Palmer had his assistants open the gates.

Another Roughneck appeared in Clobbering Claydol, wandering around the .

===== =====
Roughneck Nicky appeared briefly at the Virbank Gym in New Sword Player.

==Trivia==
In Generation I, a Cue Ball can be found swimming in . He does not appear in future generations other than Generation VII, in which he does not swim.
In and , Roughneck Kirby in the Lost Tower uses only one Pokémon; a . This is highly contradictory to the established archetype for this Trainer class, as well as his name that fans consider to .
However, he does mention that he is in the Lost Tower because his Pokémon died at the hands of Team Galactic, and Cleffa is the only one he has left.
Also, in Pokémon Platinum, one of the Roughnecks that can be fought in the expresses a dislike towards having Pokémon fight each other.
The Japanese name of this Trainer class refers to the , which is now often associated with racist and beliefs. This is likely why the name was changed for international releases.
The Cue Balls in Generation I and III use the s' overworld sprite, which, contrarily to the name of the Trainer class, depicts them with hair.
